correctness.rationale: For 1/sqrt(15)<=a<alpha, s=sqrt(1+a^2), q=4as, u=sqrt(q-1), the explicitly displayed P=(0,u-a) satisfies the lower and upper horizontal Cassinian constraints and the two vertical ones: the latter are sqrt(q(q-4a(u-a)))<=q<4s. Every three-corner triple has product 8as=2q. For r=a/s>=1/4, the squared ratio for (A,C,P) equals (1+r-sqrt(r^2+4r-1))/(1-r^2), strictly above 1 iff (r-1)((r+1)^3-2)>0, i.e. r<2^(1/3)-1; squaring is sign-safe. The increasing a->r mapping yields the exact interval and witness equality at its upper endpoint. Independent SymPy polynomial check and exact a=69/260 (s=269/260,r=69/269) reproduce strict ratio 1.020645150198... . This proves only a particular triple lower bound, not the exact global three-diameter.
